items.stem: Why can a Java generic type parameter not be used with `instanceof List<String>` at runtime?

options.text: Generic type information is erased by the compiler, so the runtime has no String parameter to check
options.rationale: Correct: type erasure removes the parameter, leaving only the raw type at runtime.

options.text: Generics are only allowed on interfaces
options.rationale: Generics apply to classes and methods too; this is unrelated.

options.text: instanceof is not a valid Java operator
options.rationale: instanceof is valid; the issue is erasure of the type argument.
List does extend Collection; this is irrelevant to the question.

items.explanation: Correct: type erasure removes the parameter, leaving only the raw type at runtime.

items.stem: Which statements about the Java Streams API are correct? (Select TWO)

options.text: A stream can be consumed by only one terminal operation
options.rationale: Correct: a stream is single-use; reusing it after a terminal op throws IllegalStateException.

options.text: Intermediate operations such as map are lazy until a terminal operation runs
options.rationale: Correct: intermediate ops build a pipeline that executes only when a terminal op is applied.

options.text: Streams always mutate the source collection in place
options.rationale: Streams do not mutate the source; they produce new results.

options.text: forEach guarantees encounter order on a parallel stream
options.rationale: Use forEachOrdered for order; forEach does not guarantee it in parallel.

items.explanation: Correct: a stream is single-use; reusing it after a terminal op throws IllegalStateException.; Correct: intermediate ops build a pipeline that executes only when a terminal op is applied.

items.stem: What is the recommended use of java.util.Optional?

options.text: As a return type to signal a possibly-absent result
options.rationale: Correct: Optional is designed for return values that may be empty.

options.text: As a field type to save memory
options.rationale: Optional is not intended for fields and adds overhead.

options.text: As a method parameter to make arguments optional
options.rationale: Using Optional parameters is discouraged; overloads are preferred.

options.text: As a replacement for all null checks everywhere
options.rationale: Optional targets return values, not a blanket null replacement.

items.explanation: Correct: Optional is designed for return values that may be empty.
